dedupe_keys.name: characterizing storm induced coastal change hazards along the united states west coast

description: Characterizing storm-induced coastal change hazards along the United States West Coast is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by James B. Shope et al. Traditional methods to assess the probability of storm-induced erosion and flooding from extreme water levels have limited use along the U.S. West Coast where swell dominates erosion and storm surge is limited. This effort presents methodology to assess the probability of erosion and flooding for the U.S. Coverage: national (US); published in 2022. Formats: CSV, TXT. The data are held in USGS ScienceBase and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
